interface.description: An actor that holds resources, takes part in economic events and makes commitments: a person, an organisation or a system (REA agent).
interface.name: core.Agent

interface.description: A role an agent plays over a period (customer, supplier, employee, carrier). A role is a relationship, not a subtype of the agent.

links.description: The agent the role is held towards, when it is not the business itself.

interface.name: core.AgentRole

interface.description: An economic claim: a right to receive resources, such as an invoice or a receivable, settled by economic events. Not a catalog claim about definitions. Disjoint from core.Commitment (Commitment ⊓ Claim = ∅): a promise is not yet a right, and no type is both. A fulfilled or accepted commitment gives rise to claims (givesRiseTo); the relation is recorded on the claim as `arises_from`, because a commitment is not edited when a claim arises.

links.description: The commitment that gave rise to the claim (givesRiseTo, seen from the claim).

interface.name: core.Claim

interface.description: A promise of a future economic event: an order line, a contract term, a subscription period. It ends fulfilled, cancelled or breached and is never dropped (DEMO request, promise, execute).

links.description: The agent that promised to give.
The agent the promise is made to.

interface.name: core.Commitment

interface.description: A posted change of resources. A transfer moves ownership or custody from provider to receiver; a transformation consumes inputs and produces outputs. Posted events are immutable; a correction is a new event that reverses its original.

links.description: The agent giving up the resource, or performing the transformation.
The agent receiving the resource; for a transformation, the agent the output belongs to.
The resource moved, consumed or produced.
The commitment this event fulfils, in whole or in part.
The posted event this event exactly reverses.

interface.name: core.EconomicEvent

interface.description: A quantity set aside against a balance: an escrow, a stock reservation or a use of a quota. A hold is released, consumed or expires, and never exceeds what is available (core.law.escrow_non_negative).

links.description: The agent the quantity is held for.
The commitment the hold secures, if any.

interface.name: core.Hold

interface.description: The value view of an economic event: one signed amount on one account. A positive amount is a debit and a negative one a credit; the side is presentation only and is never stored. The effects posted together balance (core.law.value_conservation).

links.description: The economic event this effect values.

interface.name: core.LedgerEffect

interface.description: Something of value that is conserved: goods, money, time, capacity or a right, held as a quantity in exactly one unit (a UCUM unit, or a currency for money). `valuation_method` is the governed parameter of core.law.stock_valuation (FIFO or moving average); it is null for a resource that is not valued.

links.description: The agent that owns the resource.
The agent that holds the resource, when it is not the owner.

interface.name: core.Resource

residuals.note: Internal transfers move money between one agent's own accounts; the canon has no account-to-account movement. Receive and pay entries are payments: see the member correspondences.
The stored status also has Draft, Return, Cancelled, Discounted and Internal Transfer values that outstanding amount and due date cannot produce; the canon state has no discounting state.
ERPNext lets an invoice also move stock; the canon records that as a separate transfer event.
Point-of-sale mode is a user-interface choice.
A voucher classification for ERPNext's forms.

The canon ledger entry has no debit/credit side yet.

Variant templates are an ERPNext catalogue feature.
Projected as the event's class (transfer or transformation), not as a property.
On Hold and Closed are set by users; the canon order state is derived and has no hold or close.
